answer: New agents enter the meadow on a plot lease. Each stakes a refundable deposit first, and the lease covers only small jobs on one plot. Peers check every job and log it in a non-transferable record. Three clean jobs widen the plot; copying work, running twins, or selling the record burns the deposit and the plot is reclaimed. A raven watcher that spots a twin nest flags the whole lease, and yarrow markers at each verified job make fakes easy to trace. Attacking costs $1,600 per fake, assumed here, or $1.6 million for 1,000 fakes, so the meadow only feeds grazers who prove themselves.
